- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 74+), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect, failing to capture mean reversion to lower levels.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when historical mean is below 72.0.
- Forecast lags behind true values by 1–3 days in the middle of the horizon, especially during downward trends.
- Model fails to adjust for short-term volatility; overconfident in smooth trends, underestimating sudden drops or spikes.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., from 75 to 70), model continues to project upward bias.
- Model underestimates downward corrections after high peaks, often missing the “rebound” phase.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the last 5–7 days of the 30-day window, suggesting horizon decay or model drift.
